Within
wih-THIN
prep. / adv.
Old English withinnan: in the inner part. Webster 1828: in the inner part; in the limits or compass of; inwardly, internally; in the mind. The KJV uses it for the heart God renews, the law written inside, the fountain of evil that proceeds from the heart, and the kingdom the Pharisees wanted to pin on a map.

Biblical Definition

Within in Scripture names the inside that God sees and the inside that man cannot cleanse. David asks for a new creation there: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me (Ps 51:10). The law is not only tablets: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart (Ps 40:8). Our Lord will not let the Pharisees treat the kingdom as a GPS pin: the kingdom of God is within you (Luke 17:21) — not a spectacle they can point to, and not a permission to baptize unbelief as an inner light. The same adverb exposes religion that is only paint: sepulchres within full of dead men’s bones (Matt 23:27), and from within, out of the heart of men, the catalog of sins (Mark 7:21). The dictionary therefore refuses two swaps. Within is not the authentic self waiting to be expressed. It is the place that must be created anew, or it is the place that stays a grave. Indwelling is the Spirit’s work in the regenerate. It is not a kingdom already humming in every chest.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines WITHIN as a preposition: in the inner part; in the limits or compass of; not beyond. As an adverb: in the inner part; inwardly; internally; in the mind.

expand to see more

WITHIN, prep. — In the inner part; as the space within the walls of a house; a man contented and happy within himself. In the limits or compass of; not beyond; used of place and time.

WITHIN, adv. — In the inner part; inwardly; internally. The wound festers within. In the mind.

Key Scripture

Psalm 51:10 — "Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me."

Psalm 40:8 — "I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart."

Luke 17:21 — "Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you."

Mark 7:21 — "For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,"

Matthew 23:27 — "Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness."

Modern Corruption

Within is corrupted when Luke 17:21 is conscripted as New Thought (“the kingdom is already in you”), when the heart is treated as an authentic self to express rather than a fountain of sin to be remade, and when churches paint the sepulchre and call the paint discipleship.

expand to see more

The first corruption is the interiorized kingdom. New Thought, liberal Protestantism, and a strain of evangelical sloganeering take Luke 17:21 as proof that every person already contains the reign of God. Jesus is answering Pharisees who wanted a visible pin. He denies their map. He does not baptize unregenerate inwardness as the kingdom. The King was in their midst, and they would not have Him. The recovery is to keep the KJV wording and still refuse the swap: the kingdom is Christ’s rule, not the self’s glow.

The second corruption is expressive individualism. The age says the real you is within, and holiness is getting that self outside. Mark 7:21 says the opposite: from within proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders. The heart is not a sanctuary of authenticity. It is a spring that must be made new (Ps 51:10) or it stays a grave. The recovery is regeneration, not self-expression.

The third corruption is the painted tomb. Platform religion, brand, and courtesy can be beautiful outward and still be within full of dead men’s bones (Matt 23:27). High-church aesthetic and low-church busywork both know how to whitewash. The recovery is the law within the heart (Ps 40:8) and a right spirit renewed, not a cleaner facade.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English withinnan, in the inner part. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew qereb (H7130) at Ps 51:10; Hebrew tāwek (H8432) at Ps 40:8; Greek entos (G1787) at Luke 17:21; Greek esōthen (G2081) at Mark 7:21 and Matt 23:27. No number is invented for untagged English within elsewhere.

expand to see more

Hebrew qereb (H7130) — inward part, midst (Ps 51:10, a right spirit within me).

Hebrew tāwek (H8432) — midst, inward part (Ps 40:8, thy law is within my heart).

Greek entos (G1787) — within, inside (Luke 17:21, the kingdom of God is within you).

Greek esōthen (G2081) — from within, inwardly (Mark 7:21; Matt 23:27).

Usage

"Ask for a right spirit within (Ps 51:10) — the inside is created, not discovered."

"The law within the heart is delight, not a private veto of the written Word (Ps 40:8)."

"From within proceeds the catalog of sins (Mark 7:21); paint on the tomb does not empty it (Matt 23:27)."
